newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya reformists announce budget speech protest.
newsitem.headline: Kenya reformists announce budget speech protest.

text.p: Kenyan reform leaders said on Wednesday they would march to parliament before a budget presentation on Thursday to press for constitutional reforms despite a government promise to crackdown on disruption.

Leaders of the coalition National Convention Assembly (NCA) -- which includes churches, civic groups and opposition parties -- said it wanted to present all parliament members (MPs) with copies of two NCA-sponsored reform bills the government could enact before elections later this year.

The announcement sets up the possibility of confrontation after the government of President Daniel arap Moi vowed to deploy security forces to prevent opposition protests from derailing the budget to be read by the finance minister.
Police and crack paramilitary General Service Unit troops are expected to seal off Nairobi's main commercial district.

"The call is that people should assemble around parliament around noon...and lobby their MPs before the budget starts at around 2.30 p.m. (1130 GMT)," said National Convention Executive Committee member Willy Matunga.
The NCA warned school children to avoid central Nairobi in case of violence and said it was not responsible for trouble.

President Moi, aged 73 and in power since 1978, must call presidential and parliamentary elections this year, pitting his ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) against an opposition split mainly along ethnic and personal lines.
Moi argues there is no time for such reforms before polls.

The government has instead presented to parliament the Peaceful Assemblies bill to replace the reviled Public Order Act regulating public meetings. The bill has been roundly criticised by opposition MPs who argue that the government would retain widespread power to ban meetings.
Eighteen mainly Western missions, including European Union members, the United States and Japan, welcomed the Peaceful Assemblies bill and called for dialogue ahead of elections.

"We...call upon all those involved to exercise restraint during this election period and to do everything in their power to avoid a repetition of the violence that occurred in Nairobi last month," the missions said in a statement on Tuesday.
One person died and scores of shops were looted in two days of rioting in Nairobi after security forces broke up an NCA rally on May 31. The government had declared it illegal.
Political uncertainty over the election date and the threat of violence have combined to leave forex traders nervous and investors unwilling to make long term decisions, traders said.
"We're at a very panicky stage because of the tension in the country," a foreign exchange dealer told Reuters on Wednesday.
The NCA presented to Attorney General Amos Wako its own Constitution of Kenya (Ammendment) Bill 1997 and its Statute Law (Miscellaneous Amendments) (No. 2) Bill.
The bills detail NCA demands for reform or repeal of laws it considers repressive including the Public Order Act.
